annotationRationale: The common-multiple bound forces a nontrivial greatest common divisor, whose prime factors bound the gap. A construction attains that bound.
sourceMethod: Follows the official gcd argument and construction, explicitly applying the bound to every divisor above 323 to verify that 340 is next.

review.mathCheck: For any divisor d>323, coprimality would force n≥323d>9999. Thus gcd(d,323)≥17 and divides d−323, proving d≥340. The even four-digit number 6460 has divisors 323 and 340, and the universal bound excludes intermediate divisors. Choice C is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of Q19's MAA proof on page 11. It explicitly explains the common-divisor gap and verifies that the construction attains the next-divisor bound.
review.annotationCheck: GCF and the extremal bound/construction are assessed. LCM is genuinely used through the coprime-product common-multiple argument; prime factorization appropriately supports the gap bound.
